title: [PDF] The Basel Framework - Bank for International Settlements
summary: The Basel Framework is the authoritative, comprehensive compilation of prudential standards set by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS), covering capital adequacy, risk-weighted asset calculations, market risk, counterparty credit risk, and operational risk requirements for internationally active banks. The document is structured as a reference framework organized into chapters (CAP, RBC, CRE, MAR, OPE, LEV) covering capital definition, risk-based capital requirements, credit risk approaches, market risk frameworks, operational risk, and leverage ratios. The source provides no current market intelligence, macro catalysts, or trading signals.
key_points: The Basel Framework is the complete set of BCBS prudential standards for internationally active banks, published by the Bank for International Settlements.
The framework covers capital definition (CAP), risk-based capital requirements (RBC), credit risk approaches including IRB and standardised approaches (CRE), and market risk frameworks (MAR).
Cryptoasset exposures are addressed within the framework (SCO60), indicating a regulatory treatment for crypto exposures under prudential standards.
Global systemically important banks (G-SIBs) and domestic systemically important banks (D-SIBs) have dedicated buffers specified under SCO40 and SCO50.
Counterparty credit risk sections (CRE50–CRE56) cover CCP exposures, SFT haircut floors, and capital treatment for trading book CCR.
The document is a 1982-page static reference framework (copyright BIS 2026) and not a market analysis or macro catalyst publication.
why_it_matters: This document defines the global prudential regulatory baseline for bank capital, risk-weighted assets, and market risk calculations. It is a reference standard, not an actionable market signal or current macro catalyst. Relevant for compliance, regulatory due diligence, and understanding bank capital requirements, but not for near-term market structure or macro catalyst research.
market_structure_context: The Basel Framework establishes the structural prudential requirements governing bank capital, market risk (MAR), counterparty credit risk (CRE50–CRE56), and leverage ratios (LEV) that define permissible market activity and risk-taking capacity. This is a structural regulatory foundation, not a current market operations or market structure analysis.
